name: City on the Thames: A Biography of London
description: Nearly two thousand years of London, from a Roman trading post to a world capital, through plague, fire, empire, bombs, pop and Brexit.

checkpoints.name: From Londinium to the Normans
checkpoints.note: The Romans found Londinium by the Thames, and over the centuries the city becomes a trading port. By the end of the period a church is rising at Westminster, where kings will be crowned in Westminster Abbey.

checkpoints.name: Medieval city
checkpoints.note: The Normans raise the Tower of London, the barons force King John to sign Magna Carta, and the Black Death empties the streets. By Shakespeare's day plays are staged at the Globe.

checkpoints.name: Plague, fire and rebuilding
checkpoints.note: The East India Company, the Royal Society and the British Museum show London as a place of trade, science and learning. The Great Plague and the Great Fire of London strike, and Samuel Pepys records them. Wren rebuilds St Paul's, and the Bank of England and The Times appear.

checkpoints.name: Imperial capital
checkpoints.note: London becomes the biggest city in the world. Dickens writes of its poor, the Thames Tunnel, Underground, Great Exhibition in the Crystal Palace and Tower Bridge show its ambition, the Broad Street cholera outbreak leads to cleaner water, and Sherlock Holmes and Peter Pan are born in its streets.

checkpoints.name: War, pop and carnival
checkpoints.note: The BBC begins broadcasting, and in the Second World War London endures the Blitz and the Battle of Britain is fought overhead under Winston Churchill. The Great Smog of 1952 hits. After Elizabeth II's coronation the Beatles at Abbey Road, punk and the Notting Hill Carnival remake its culture.

checkpoints.name: Global London
checkpoints.note: The 2012 Olympics show a diverse, confident capital, and the Brexit vote of 2016 sets a new relationship with Europe.
